answers.explanation: printf() is a library function. It runs in user mode before any trap.
The number selects the table entry; the parameters go in registers, a block, or the stack.
From chapter 1: a system call is a trap that sets the mode bit to kernel.
Number in, table lookup, implementation out.
Status and return values travel back up the same path.
That's exactly the fallback your api_call() used.
The library call wraps the system call.
The API stays the same; what's underneath it differs. That's the portability benefit.
